senses.gloss:
दंश् 1. दंश्, cl. 1. 10. P. दंशति, दंश-
यति, &c., to speak or shine.

दंश् 2. दंश्, cl. 1. P. (ep. also A.) द-
शति, -ते, ददंश, दङ्क्ष्यति (ep. also
दंशिष्यति), अदाङ्क्षीत्, दंष्टुम्, to bite, sting;
to see [? cf. rt. दंस्]: Caus. P. दंशयति, -यितुम्,
Aor. अददङ्क्षत्, to cause to bite; to bite: Desid.
दिदङ्क्षति: Intens. दन्दश्यते, दन्दंष्टि,
दन्दष्टि: Caus. of Intens. दन्दशयति, to cause
to bite violently; [cf. Gr. δάκνω, δάκος, ὀδαγμός,
ὀδάζω, ὀδακτάζω, ὀδαξέω, &c., δάκρυ; Lat. la-
cruma, perhaps lacero; Goth. tahyan, ‘dilacerate,’
tagr; Angl. Sax. taeher, tux, tusk, tang; Old Germ.
zanga, zangar; Cambro-Brit. danhezu, ‘to bite;’
Hib. dan-t, ‘a morsel, portion, share;’ Russ. desnà,
‘ginger.’]

दंश, अस्, m. biting, stinging; cutting, dividing,
tearing; the sting of a snake; a bite, the spot bitten;
pungency; fault, defect (in a jewel &c.); a tooth; a
gad-fly; armour, a coat of mail; a joint, limb; N. of
an Asura; (ई), f. a small gad-fly; [cf. क्षमा-द्˚ and वृ-
ष-द्˚.]
—दंश-नाशिनी, f. (‘healing irritation of the
skin ?’), a kind of insect, = तैल-कीट; [cf. दर्द्रु-
नाशिनी.]
—दंश-भीरु, उस्, m. or दंश-भीरुक,
अस्, m. ‘afraid of the gad-fly,’ a buffalo.
—दंश-मूल,
अस्, m. ‘having a pungent root,’ the plant Hyperanthera
Moringa or a sort of horse-radish, = शिग्रु.
—दंश-
वदन, अस्, m. ‘having a sharp beak,’ a heron.

दंशन, अम्, n. the act of biting, stinging;
armour, mail.

दंसन, अम्, आ, n. f. (Ved. inst. दंसना),
a surprising or wonderful deed or operation, mar-
vellous power; an action, work, deed; armour,
mail, (in the latter meaning only a various reading
for दंशन); [cf. दस्म and दस्र.]
—दं-
सना-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. having wonderful power;
(Sāy.) abounding in marvellous deeds.

दंशित, अस्, आ, अम्, bitten, stung; (fr. दंश),
armed, mailed; protected; fitting closely (like armour),
standing closely together, crowded; (अम्), n. a bite;
[cf. परि-दंशित.]

दंशिन्, ई, इनी, इ, biting, stinging [cf. तृप्र-
दंशिन्]; (ई), m. a dog; a gad-fly, a wasp.
दंशुक, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. biting, stinging.

दंशेर, अस्, आ, अम् (more correctly दशेर,
q. v.), biting, mordacious; noxious, mischievous.
दंश्मन्, अ, n., Ved. a bite; the place bitten.
दंष्टृ, टा, ट्री, टृ, Ved. a biter, biting, stinging.

दंष्ट्र, अस्, आ, m. f. (in the later language
usually f.), a large tooth, tusk, fang, (often at the
end of comp.; cf. अयो-द्˚, अष्ट-द्˚, तीक्ष्ण-द्˚,
&c.)
—दंष्ट्रा-कराल, अस्, आ, अम्, having terrible
tusks.
—दंष्ट्रा-निवासिन्, ई, m., N. of a Yakṣas.
—दंष्ट्रायुध (˚रा-आय्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, using
tusks as weapons; (अस्), m. a wild boar.
—दंष्-
ट्रा-सेन, अस्, m., N. of a Buddhist scholar.

दंष्ट्राल, अस्, आ, अम्, tusked, having large
tusks; (अस्), m., N. of a Rākṣasa.

दंष्ट्रिन्, ई, इणी, इ, tusked, having tusks or
large teeth; biting or wounding with the teeth;
carnivorous; (ई), m. any animal with tusks; a wild
boar; a hyena; a snake.
दंष्ट्वा, ind. having bitten.

दंसयितृ, ता, m. a destroyer, (a word formed
to explain दस्र.)

दंसस्, अस्, n., Ved. = दंसन, a surprising
action or deed (applied especially to the wonderful
actions of the Aśvins, by which these deities pro-
tected their human friends); [cf. पुरु-द्˚ and सु-द्˚.]
दंसि, इस्, m. f. (?), Ved. = कर्मन्, act, deed.

दंसिष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम् (superl. of दंसु or द-
स्र), Ved. of very wonderful strength, performing
marvellous deeds, eminent in action, epithet of the
Aśvins and of Indra.

दंसु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. of wonderful strength;
(according to Sāy., loc. of दम् = दंसेषु or कर्-
म-वत्सु); (उ), ind. in a wonderful way, wonder-
fully.
—दंसु-जूत, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. wonderfully
quick; (Sāy.) borne along by well-trained horses (as
if fr. rt. 1. दम्).
—दंसु-पत्नी, f., Ved. having a
powerful lord or master; (Sāy.) having the Asuras
as good masters (as if fr. दम् + सु + पत्नी, सु =
सुष्ठु); in Ṛg-veda VI. 3, 7, दम् is regarded
as a separate word.

दंह् दंह्, cl. 10. P. दंहयति, &c., to
shine, burn; [cf. rt. 1. दह्.]

दंक्ष्णु दङ्क्ष्णु, उस्, उस्, उ (fr. rt. 2. दंश्),
Ved. biting, mordaceous.

दन् 1. दन्, Ved., explained by Sāyaṇa as
a participle fr. rt. 1. दा = ददत् or दातृ, giving,
bestowing; modern scholars connect this word with
पति and explain पतिर्-दम् as a transposition of
दम्-पति, q. v.

दन् 2. दन्, considered by some as a Vedic
root, from which they derive the Desid. दीदांसते
(referred by Pāṇ. III. 1, 6, to rt. दान्, q. v.) and
other forms; the meaning is said to be straight, to
straighten; to correct. (In Ṛg-veda I. 174, 2,
[]
दनस् is said by Yāska to = दान-मनसस्, liberal-
minded, disposed to give, see Nirukta VI. 31; but
according to Sāy., दनस् = अदमयस्, thou hast
humbled, or by transposition of the letters अन-
दस्.)

दान् दान्, cl. 1. P. A. or cl. 10. P. दान-
यति, &c., to cut off: Desid. P. A. दीदं-
सति, -ते, to straighten, make straight; to be straight;
(this verb is by some regarded as a nominal fr. 2.
दान; cf. 2. दन्.)

दनायुस् दनायुस्, उस्, f., N. of one of the
daughters of Dakṣa, married to Kaśyapa; (ऊस्),
m. (?), N. of the supposed father (?) of the Dānavas;
[cf. दनु.]

दनीध्वंस दनीध्वंस, an adj. formed fr.
Intens. of rt. ध्वंस्.

दनु दनु, उस्, f., N. of one of the daughters
of Dakṣa, wife of Kaśyapa, and mother of the
demons called Dānavas, the Titans of Hindū mytho-
logy; the number of these Dānavas is stated to be
40 in Mahā-bh. 1. 252, but 100 &c. are reckoned
in other places; (उस्), m., N. of a son of Śrī, also
called Dānava; (he was originally very handsome,
but having offended Indra, was changed by him into
a deformed monster; see कबन्ध.)
—दनु-ज,
अस्, or दनु-सम्भव, अस्, or दनु-सूनु, उस्, m.
a son of Danu, a Dānava.
—दनुज-द्विष्, ट्, or
दनुजारि (˚ज-अरि), इस्, m. an enemy of the Dānavas,
a god, a deity.

1. दानु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. liberal; a donor, giver;
prosperity, contentment; air, wind.

2. दानु, उस्, उस्, उ (for 1. see p. 407, col. 3), valiant;
a victor, conqueror, destroyer; (उस्), m. a class of
demons; (उ), n. a fluid, a drop, dew; [cf. आर्द्र-द्˚,
जीर-द्˚.]
—दानु-चित्र, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. shining
with dew, brilliant with moisture; (Sāy.) wonderfully
destructive, wonderfully liberal, marvellous by gifts,
(as if fr. 1. दा.)
—दानु-द, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. giving
drops, trickling.
—दानुनस्-पती, m. du. (fr. the
gen. sing. of 2. दानु), Ved. ‘the lords of dew,’ epithet
of Mitra-varuṇa and of the Aśvins; (Sāy.) lords of
munificence, (as if fr. 1. दा.)
—दानु-पिन्व, अस्,
[]
&c., Ved. swelling with drops.
—दानु-मत्, आन्,
अती, अत्, Ved. having many oblations; liquid, fluid,
trickling; (Sāy.) malignant, injurious; having gifts,
liberal, suited to a giver, (as if fr. 1. दा.)
दनुष, अस्, m. (?) a Rākṣasa.

दन्त दन्त, अस्, m. (for etym. see दत्, p. 399,
col. 2), a tooth, tusk, fang; an elephant's tusk, ivory;
the point of an arrow; the peak of a mountain, the
side or ridge of a mountain; (ई), f. a medicinal plant
yielding a pungent oil, commonly Danti, Croton
Polyandrum or Croton Tiglium [cf. दन्त-मूलिका
and दन्तिनी]; at the end of an adj. comp. the fem.
of दन्त may end in आ or ई; [cf. इभ-दन्ता,
कुड्मल-दन्ती, क्रूर-दन्ती, &c.: cf. also Zend
dañt-an, ‘tooth;’ Gr. ἀ-δούς, ὀ-δοντ Æol. pl.
ἔδοντες; Lat. dens; Lith. dant-i-s; Goth. tunth-
u-s; Angl. Sax. todh; Old Germ. zant, zand, zan;
Cambro-Brit. dant; Hib. déad.]
—दन्त-कर्-
षण, अस्, ई, अम्, contracting the teeth, i. e. setting
them on edge; (अस्), m. the common lime, Citrus
Acida.
—दन्त-कार, अस्, m. an artist who works
in ivory.
—दन्त-काष्ठ, अम्, n. a piece of stick
or small twig of particular trees used as a tooth-brush
or chewed to cleanse the teeth; cleaning the teeth
in this manner; (अस्), m., N. of various trees, the
wood of which is used for cleaning the teeth; Fla-
courtia Sapida (= वि-कङ्कत); Asclepias Gigantea;
Ficus Indica (= वट); Acacia Catechu; Pongamia
Glabra; Terminalia Alata; [cf. दन्त-धावन.]
—दन्त-काष्ठक, अस्, m. the shrub Tabernæ-
montana Coronaria (= आहुल्य).
—दन्तकाष्ठा-
भक्षण (˚ठ-अ-भ्˚), अम्, n., N. of the 128th
chapter of the Vārāha-Purāṇa.
—दन्त-कुमार,
अस्, m., N. of a man.
—दन्त-क्रूरम्, ind. cruelly
or fearfully on the teeth, fearfully with or by the
teeth (e. g. to seize or strike a person in this man-
ner).
—दन्तग्राहि-ता, f. the state of causing injury
to the teeth.
—दन्त-ग्राहिन्, ई, इणी, इ, injuring
the teeth, causing them to decay &c.
—दन्त-
घर्ष, अस्, m. chattering or grinding of the teeth;
[cf. दन्त-सङ्घर्ष and दन्त-हर्ष.]
—दन्-
त-घात, अस्, m. ‘a blow with the teeth,’ a bite
[cf. दन्त-विघात]; N. of a man.
—दन्त-चाल,
अस्, m. looseness of the teeth.
—दन्त-च्छद,
अस्, m. ‘the covering of the teeth,’ a lip [cf. दच्-
छद and दशन-च्छद]; (आ), f. Momordica
Monadelpha.
—दन्तच्छदोपमा (˚द-उप्˚), f.
Momordica Monadelpha, (to the red fruit of which
the lips are often compared.)
—दन्त-जात = जात-
दन्त, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘having teeth,’ a child who is teeth-
ing or whose teeth are just appearing; (अ-दन्तजात,
having no teeth.)
—दन्त-जाह, अम्, n. the root
of a tooth.
—दन्त-दर्शन, अम्, n. showing the
teeth (as a dog does).
—दन्त-धावन, अम्, n.
cleaning or washing the teeth; a tooth-brush or
fibrous stick for cleaning the teeth, or a piece of
wood chewed for that purpose [cf. दन्त-काष्ठ];
(अस्), m., N. of various trees, the wood of which is
[]
used for cleaning the teeth, Acacia Catechu, Mimu-
sops Elengi (= वकुल); N. of a chapter of the
Purāṇa-sarva-sva by Halāyudha.
—दन्तधाव-
नक, अस्, m. a species of tree.
—दन्तधावन-
प्रकरण, अम्, n., N. of a chapter of the Parā-
śara-smṛti-vyākhyā by Mādhava.
—दन्तधावन-
विधि, इस्, m., N. of a chapter of the Smṛti-kau-
mudī.
—दन्त-पत्त्र, अम्, n. a kind of ear-ring.
—दन्त-पत्त्रक, अम्, n. a kind of jasmine (=
कुन्द), Jasminum Pubescens, (the petals or leaves
of the flower resembling teeth in colour and shape,
and are often so compared in poetry.)
—दन्त-
पवन, अम्, n. a dentifrice, or a small piece of
wood taken to clean the teeth; [cf. दन्त-काष्ठ
and दन्त-धावन.]
—दन्त-पात, अस्, m. the
falling out of the teeth.
—दन्त-पाली, f. the gum.
—दन्त-पुप्पुट or दन्त-पुप्पुटक, अस्, m.
gum-boil.
—दन्त-पुर, अम्, n. ‘the town of Bud-
dha's tooth,’ N. of the capital of the Kaliṅgas.
—दन्त-पुष्प, अस्, m. the plant Strychnos Po-
tatorum, the flower of which is compared to a tooth;
(अम्), n. the fruit of the above plant.
—दन्त-
प्रक्षालन, अम्, n. cleaning the teeth; any in-
strument or means for cleaning the teeth; [cf. दन्-
त-काष्ठ, दन्त-धावन, दन्त-पवन.]
—दन्त-फल, अस्, m. Feronia Elephantum, =
कपित्थ [cf. दधि-फल]; (आ), f. long pepper;
(अम्), n. = दन्त-पुष्प, q. v.
—दन्त-भङ्ग,
अस्, m. fracture of the teeth.
—दन्त-भाग, अस्,
m. the fore part of an elephant's head (where the
tusks appear); part of a tooth.
—दन्त-मय, अस्,
ई, अम्, made of ivory.
—दन्त-मल, अम्, n. the
tartar of the teeth, any impurity of the teeth.
—दन्त-मांस, अम्, n. the gums.
—दन्त-
मूल, अम्, n. the root of a tooth, the gums; a gum-
boil.
—दन्त-मूलिका, f. = दन्ती, Croton Polyan-
drum or Croton Tiglium.
—दन्तमूलीय, अस्, आ,
अम्, belonging to the root of the teeth, as the dental
letters; दन्तमूलीयस् त-कार-वर्गस्, the class of
letters beginning with त which are uttered from the
root of the teeth.
—दन्त-रजस्, अस्, n. the tartar of
the teeth, impurity of the teeth.
—दन्त-रोग, अस्,
m. disease of the teeth, tooth-ache.
—दन्तरोगिन्,
ई, इणी, इ, affected with tooth-ache.
—दन्त-लेख-
क, अस्, m. one who makes a livelihood by painting
or marking the teeth.
—दन्त-लोक, अस्, m., N. of a
mountain in Gāndhāra.
—दन्त-वक्त्र, अस्, m., N.
of a prince of the Karūṣas (described as a Dānava or
Asura; more correctly दन्त-वक्र).
—दन्त-वत्,
आन्, अती, अत्, having teeth, toothed.
—दन्त-वल्क,
अम्, n. the enamel of the teeth.
—दन्त-वस्त्र,
अम्, n. (according to some also अस्, m.), ‘teeth-
covering,’ i. e. the lip.
—दन्त-वासस्, आस् (?), अस्, m. (?)
n. the lip; see the preceding.
—दन्त-विघात,
अस्, m. = दन्त-घात, a bite.
—दन्त-वीज, अस्,
आ, m. f. and दन्त-वीजक, अस्, m. pomegranate;
(आ), f. a kind of cucumber.
—दन्त-वीणा, f. ‘a
tooth-guitar,’ a kind of jew's-harp; (दन्त-वीणां
वादयत्, playing this instrument; in Pañca-tantra
94, 4, = making a chattering with the teeth.)
—दन्-
त-वेष्ट, अस्, m. the gums; (औ), m. du. the
gums of the upper and lower jaw; a ring round
the tusk of an elephant (?) ; tumor of the gums;
see the next.
—दन्त-वेष्टक, अस्, m. tumor of
the gums (internal abscess accompanied with loosening
of the teeth), gum-boil.
—दन्त-वैदर्भ, अस्, m.
loosening of the teeth through external injury.
—दन्त-व्यसन, अम्, n. fracture or decay of the
teeth or of a tusk.
—दन्त-शङ्कु, उ, n. a pair of
forceps or pincers for drawing teeth.
—दन्त-शट,
अस्, m. a wrong form for दन्त-शठ.
—दन्त-
शठ, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘bad for the teeth,’ acid; (अस्),
m. sourness, acidity; N. of several trees with acid
fruits; common lime (Citrus Acida), elephant or
wood-apple, Feronia Elephantum, Averrhoa Caram-
bola (Acida), Citrus Aurantium; (आ), f. wood-sorrel,
Oxalis Pusilla, = क्षुद्राम्लिका; (अम्), n. the fruits
of the above trees.
—दन्त-शर्करा, f. tartar or
concretion of the teeth.
—दन्त-शाण, अम्, n. a
dentifrice composed chiefly of the powdered fruit of
the myrobalan and green sulphate of iron.
—दन्त-
[]
शिरा, f. a back or double tooth (= माढी); the
gum.
—दन्त-शुद्धि, इस्, f. cleaning the teeth.
—दन्त-शूल, अस्, अम्, m. n. tooth-ache.
—दन्त-
शोधनी, f. ‘tooth-cleanser,’ a tooth-pick.
—दन्त-
शोफ, अस्, m. swelling of the gum.
—दन्त-श्लि-
ष्ट or दन्त-सक्त, अस्, आ, अम्, entangled in or
between the teeth.
—दन्त-सङ्घर्ष, अस्, m.
rubbing the teeth together, gnashing the teeth;
[cf. दन्त-घर्ष and दन्त-हर्ष.]
—दन्त-
हर्ष, अस्, m. morbid sensitiveness of the teeth,
intolerance of any rough or acid substances; chat-
tering of the teeth; [cf. दन्त-घर्ष and दन्त-
सङ्घर्ष.]
—दन्त-हर्षक or दन्त-हर्-
षण, अस्, m. ‘making the teeth sensitive, setting
them on edge,’ the lime tree, Citrus Acida.
—दन्त-
हीन, अस्, आ, अम्, toothless.
—दन्ताग्र (˚त-अग्˚),
अम्, n. the top or point of a tooth.
—दन्ताघात
(˚त-आघ्˚), अस्, m. ‘tooth-blow’ or ‘tooth-wound,’
a bite; the citron or lime tree.
—दन्ताघातिन्, ई,
इनी, इ, struck with the teeth, bitten, remaining
between the teeth.
—दन्ताद (˚त-अद्˚), अस्, आ,
अम्, corroding the teeth.
—दन्ता-दन्ति, ind. tooth
against tooth, i. e. biting one another.
—दन्तान्तर
(˚त-अन्˚), अम्, n. the space between the teeth.
—दन्तान्तराधिष्ठित (˚र-अध्˚), अस्, आ, अम्,
sticking between the teeth.
—दन्तायुध (˚त-
आय्˚), अस्, m. a wild boar, a hog (‘having tusks for
weapons’).
—दन्तार्बुद (˚त-अर्˚), अस्, अम्, m. n.
gum-boil, ulceration of the gums.
—दन्तालय (˚त-
आल्˚), अस्, m. ‘the abode of the teeth,’ i. e. the
mouth.
—दन्तालिका or दन्ताली (˚त-आल्˚), f. a
horse's bridle or bit; [cf. 1. आलि.]
—दन्तोच्-
छिष्ट (˚त-उच्˚), अम्, n. the remains of food
lodged between the teeth.
—दन्तोद्भेद (˚त-उद्˚),
अस्, m. appearance of the teeth, dentition.
—दन्तो-
लूखलिक, अस्, आ, अम्, or दन्तोलूखलिन् (˚त-उल्˚),
ई, इनी, इ, ‘one who uses his teeth as a mortar,’ one
who grinds his grain between the teeth, i. e. eats it
before being ground, an anchorite.
—दन्तोष्ठक
(˚त-ओष्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, one who attends to or takes
care of his teeth and lips.

दान्त 2. दान्त, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. दन्त), dental,
made of ivory; ‘completed by Danta (?),’ epithet of a
well situated on the northern or southern bank of the
river Vipāśā; (see Pāṇ. IV. 2, 74, Schol.)

दन्तक = दन्त, a tooth &c. (at the end of a
comp., cf. अ-दन्तक, कृमि-द्˚, श्याव-द्˚); (अस्),
m. a jagged peak or projection in a rock or moun-
tain; a bracket, a pin or shelf projecting from a
wall; (अस्, आ, अम्), paying attention to one's teeth.

दन्तावल or दन्ताबल, अस्, m. an elephant
(? for दन्त-वल = दन्तिन्).

दन्ति, इस्, m. (probably) an epithet of Gaṇeśa;
[cf. एक-दन्त.]

दन्ती, f. the plant Croton Polyandrum; see above
under दन्त; [cf. दन्तिका and दन्तिजा.]
—दन्ती-
वीज, अम्, n. a strongly purgative nut, the fruit of
the Croton.

दान्ति, इस्, f. self-restraint; the patient endurance
of religious austerities or privations; subjection, hu-
miliation.

दन्तिका or दन्तिजा = दन्ती below; [cf. गुच्छ-
दन्तिका.]
दान्तिक, अस्, ई, अम्, made of ivory.

दन्तिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having teeth, toothed, tusked;
(ई), m. an elephant; a mountain; (इनी), f. = दन्ती
below.
—दन्ति-दन्त, अस्, m. an elephant's tusk,
ivory.
—दन्तिदन्त-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, made of
ivory.
—दन्ति-मद, अस्, m. the juice flowing from
the temples of a rutting elephant.
दन्तिल, अस्, m., N. of a man.

दन्तुर, अस्, आ, अम्, having long or projecting
teeth; jagged, notched, serrated, uneven; waving,
undulatory; rising (as hair), bristling.
—दन्तुर-
च्छद, अस्, m. the lime tree (‘having prickly leaves’).

दन्तुरित, अस्, आ, अम्, having prominent teeth,
toothed, notched, bristling.

दन्तूल, अस्, आ, अम्, having teeth, furnished with
teeth.

दन्त्य, अस्, आ, अम्, dental, of or belonging to
the teeth, produced on the teeth; suitable to the
teeth; [cf. अ-द्˚.]
—दन्त्योष्ठ्य or दन्त्यौ-
ष्ठ्य (˚य-ओष्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, denti-labial.
दन्तकूर दन्तकूर, N. of a place.

दन्दश दन्दश, अस्, m. (fr. Intens. of rt.
2. दंश्), a tooth.

दन्दशूक, अस्, आ, अम्, mordacious, biting, mis-
chievous, malignant, venomous; (अस्), m. a snake,
serpent; a particular kind of serpent; N. of a hell
infested by serpents; a Rākṣasa, a demon or goblin.

दन्द्रम दन्द्रम, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. Intens. of
rt. द्रम्), going tortuously or slowly (?).

दन्द्रमण, अम्, n. the act of going tortu-
ously; (अस्, आ, अम्), who or what goes tortuously.

1. दान, अस्, m., Ved. a giver, giving; an offering,
(according to Sāy. = दत्त or देय-भूत, but
thought by modern scholars to be the epithet of a
horse); (अम्), n. giving, presenting; giving in
marriage (e. g. कन्या-द्˚, q. v.); giving up, sacri-
ficing (e. g. प्राण-द्˚, q. v.); delivering, distributing;
communicating, imparting, teaching, giving instruc-
tion (e. g. ब्रह्म-द्˚, q. v.); a gift, present, donation
(e. g. दानं दा, to offer a gift; cf. Lat. donum);
special gift, oblation (e. g. उदक-द्˚, q. v.); adding,
addition; liberality; bribery (one of the four means
by which a king overpowers his enemies; cf. उपाय);
the fragrant fluid that flows from the temples of an
elephant in rut (more probably connected with rt. 3. दा;
see 2. दान, p. 408, col. 1); a kind of honey, (per-
haps for दाल.)
—दान-कल्प-तरु, उस्, m., N. of a
work mentioned in the Saṃskāra-tattva by Raghu-
nandana.
—दान-काम, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. fond of
giving, liberal.
—दान-कुल्या, f. the flow of fluid from
an elephant's temples.
—दान-कुसुमाञ्जलि (˚म-
अञ्˚), N. of a poem.
—दान-कौमुदी, f., N. of the
second part of the Kriyā-kaumudī.
—दान-च्युत, अस्,
m., N. of a man.
—दान-तस्, ind. through gifts, by
liberality.
—दान-दर्पण, N. of a work mentioned
in the Saṃskāra-tattva.
—दान-धर्म, अस्, m. alms-
giving, charitable acts, charity; the rules or practice
[]
of alms-giving.
—दानधर्म-विधि, इस्, m. ‘the
rules for alms-giving &c.,’ N. of a chapter of the
Skanda-Purāṇa.
—दान-पति, इस्, m. ‘a master of
liberality,’ an exceedingly liberal or munificent man;
an epithet of A-krūra, who was kinsman of Kṛṣṇa;
N. of a Daitya.
—दान-पत्त्र, अम्, n. a deed of
gift or conveyance.
—दान-पद्धति, इस्, f., N. of
a work on the sixteen chief oblations.
—दान-पात्र,
अम्, n. ‘an object of charity, one who deserves a gift,’
N. of a chapter of the Purāṇa-sarva-sva.
—दान-
प्रतिभाव्य, अम्, n. security for payment of a debt
&c.
—दान-भिन्न, अस्, आ, अम्, divided or made
hostile by bribes.
—दान-योग्य, अस्, आ, अम्, worthy
of a gift, meriting a donation.
—दान-वज्र, अस्,
&c., ‘whose thunderbolt is liberality,’ an epithet of
the Vaiśyas or men of the third tribe.
—दान-वत्,
आन्, अती, अत्, having gifts, presenting gifts, liberal.
—दान-विधि, इस्, m., N. of a chapter of the
Skanda-Purāṇa.
—दान-वीर, अस्, m. ‘a hero in
liberality,’ an exceedingly liberal man.
—दान-व्य-
त्यास, अस्, m. ‘perversion of gifts,’ gift under error,
giving to the wrong person.
—दान-व्रत, अस्, आ,
अम्, devoted to liberality or benevolence; (आस्), m.
pl. the inhabitants of Śāka-dvīpa.
—दान-शील, अस्,
आ, अम्, liberally disposed, liberal, generous, charitable,
munificent; (अस्), m., N. of one of the translators
of the Lalita-vistara in Tibetian.
—दान-शूर, अस्,
m. ‘a hero in liberality,’ N. of a Bodhi-sattva (=
Śākya-muni in a former birth; cf. दान-वीर).
—दा-
न-शौण्ड, अस्, ई, अम्, ‘intoxicated with giving,’ ex-
ceedingly liberal.
—दान-सागर, अस्, m. ‘the ocean
of gifts,’ N. of a work by Malamāsa mentioned
in the Saṃskāra-tattva by Raghu-nandana.
—दा-
न-स्तुति, इस्, f. ‘praise of liberality,’ N. of a kind of
hymn.
—दान-हीन, अस्, आ, अम्, deprived of gifts.
—दान-हेमाद्रि (˚म-अद्˚), N. of a work on
oblations written under the patronage of Hemādri.
—दानाधिकार (˚न-अध्˚), अस्, m., N. of a short
Buddhist work on alms-giving.

2. दान, अस्, m. (for 1. दान see p. 407, col. 2),
Ved. distribution (especially of food); a meal; a sacri-
ficial meal; distributing, communicating, liberality;
part, share, possession; a distributer; (अम्), n. cut-
ting off, dividing; pasture; the fluid flowing from
an elephant's temples when in rut; [cf. 1. दान.]
—दानाप्नस् (˚न-अप्˚), आस्, आस्, अस्, Ved. having
abundant shares (or gifts, fr. 1. दान).
—दानौकस्
(˚न-ओक्˚), आस्, m., Ved. delighting in the sacrificial
meal; (Sāy.) ‘the abode of liberality, munificent,’
epithet of Indra, (as if fr. 1. दान.)
3. दान, अम्, n. purification; [cf. 1. अव-दान.]
दान दान, &c. See under rts. 1. and 3. दा.
दानक, अम्, n. a mean, paltry, or miserable gift.

दानिक, (at the end of comp.) relating or referring
to a gift, liberality, giving instruction, &c. (e. g.
अध्ययन-द्˚, consisting in the giving of instruction
or in reading; cf. वर-द्˚ and उदक-द्˚).

दानिन्, ई, इनी, इ, giving, liberal, benevolent; hav-
ing gifts; [cf. अग्र-द्˚.]

दानीय, अस्, आ, अम्, due, bestowable, worthy or
fit to be given; receiving gifts or oblations; (अम्),
n. a thing to be given, gift, donation.

दानव, अस्, ई, m. f. a class of demons, a giant,
a Titan; (according to a later conception the Dānavas,
who are implacable enemies of the Devas, are children
of Danu and Kaśyapa, see दनु, p. 401; the Daityas
and Dānavas are often identified, and both of them
are called Asuras); (अस्, ई, अम्), belonging to the
Dānavas, peculiar to the Dānavas, &c.
—दानव-
गुरु, उस्, m. ‘the preceptor of the Dānavas,’ N. of
the regent of the planet Venus.
—दानव-पति, इस्,
m. the king of the Dānavas.
—दानव-पूजित, अस्,
आ, अम्, worshipped by the Dānavas; (अस्), m. the
regent of the planet Venus.
—दानव-प्रिया, f. the
betel plant.
—दानव-सूदन, अस्, आ, अम्, destroy-
ing the Dānavas.
—दानवारि (˚व-अरि), इस्, m. an
enemy of the Dānavas; an epithet of Indra; of
Śiva; (अयस्), m. pl. the gods.
—दानवेन्द्र (˚व-
इन्˚), अस्, m. the chief of the Dānavas.
दानव दानव. See दानु.
दानवेय, अस्, m. a Dānava or demon.
दान्त्वा, ind. having subdued, tamed, &c.

दन्ध्वन, अस्, m. (fr. Intens. of rt. 2. ध्वन्),
‘sounding very much,’ a kind of reed or cane.
